question: Who among the following had given the idea to mobilise all the leading Indian political leaders under a common platform called the Indian National Congress?
solution:
The correct answer is __**A O Hume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A O Hume** is credited with the idea of mobilizing leading Indian political leaders under a common platform, which later became the **Indian National Congress (INC)**.
 
• He was a retired British civil servant and was motivated by his belief that an organized platform for Indians would help address their grievances and prevent potential unrest against British rule.
 
• Hume's efforts culminated in the first session of the **Indian National Congress**, which was held in **Bombay (now Mumbai)** in December **1885**. *Hence, the correct option is A O Hume.*
 
• The founding of the INC marked a significant moment in the Indian freedom struggle, as it provided a platform for Indians to voice their political and social concerns.
 
• Hume's initiative was supported by other early leaders like **W C Bannerjee**, who became the first president of INC, along with **Surendranath Bannerjee** and **Ananda Mohan Bose**, who were prominent leaders in the Indian political sphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A O Hume and the Formation of INC:**

 
 
• **Allan Octavian Hume** was a British administrator and reformer. He believed that providing a political platform for Indians would help establish a dialogue between the British administration and Indian society.
 
• Hume acted as a mediator between Indians and the British government, ensuring that political demands were conveyed peacefully.
 
• His initiative led to the first session of the INC in **December 1885**, with **72 delegates** attending the meeting.
 
 
 
• **Role of Other Leaders:**
 
 
• **W C Bannerjee** was the first president of INC and played a crucial role in shaping the early objectives of the organization.
 
• **Surendranath Bannerjee** was a prominent nationalist leader and was involved in early political movements like the Indian Association, which later merged with the INC.
 
• **Ananda Mohan Bose** was an advocate of Indian self-rule and contributed significantly to the political discourse at the time.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of the Indian National Congress:**
 
 
• The INC was established to promote political awareness and unity among Indians and to act as a platform for articulating their demands.
 
• Initially, its demands were moderate, focusing on administrative reforms, representation in government, and safeguarding Indian interests.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Contributions of A O Hume:**

 
 
• A O Hume's efforts in organizing the INC are considered instrumental in laying the foundation for India's freedom movement.
 
• He emphasized non-violent methods and negotiation as tools for achieving political goals.
 
• Though a British civil servant, Hume's sympathy towards Indian causes earned him respect among early nationalist leaders.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of the INC:**
 
 
• The INC eventually became the primary organization leading the Indian independence movement, with leaders like **Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru,** and **Sardar Patel**.
 
• It evolved from a moderate organization into a mass movement demanding complete independence from British rule.
